ambiguities.description: The text requires responses to be received at the "location indicated above", but no physical or electronic submission location or portal is stated in this chunk, so the bidder cannot tell where to deliver the proposal.

The RFP says the preferred Vendor shall have experience implementing solutions for cities of similar size and scope, but neither 'similar size' nor 'scope of services' is defined, so bidders cannot tell whether their references qualify; the bidder would ask what population/budget threshold and which service areas count.

Best-of-breed HCM vendors are invited to respond, but it is unclear whether such a response must also cover the full ERP scope or only the HCM functionality, and whether the City will contract with multiple vendors; the bidder would ask what the minimum required scope of a best-of-breed response is.

The text requires the solution to include the modules and functionality in the Requirements document but does not state whether those requirements are mandatory pass/fail or scored, nor whether deviations may be proposed; a bidder would ask how compliance is evaluated and whether alternative functionality is acceptable.

The implementation approach is left open (phased or vendor-recommended and City-approved) with no stated timeline, milestones or approval process; a bidder would ask what schedule constraints and approval gates apply.

The City reserves the right to modify or reschedule the timeline, so the bidder cannot know whether the stated dates (e.g., the September 17, 2024 proposal deadline or the March 2025 implementation start) are firm; the bidder would ask how much notice will be given for changes and whether pricing must hold to the stated dates.

The Go Live date of January 1, 2027 is stated as an evaluation criterion, but it is unclear whether it is a firm contractual deadline or merely a scored factor, and whether it applies to all modules including any phased rollout. The bidder would ask whether the date is binding and what happens if it slips.

The text refers to a Demo Script document that will be provided to finalists and to pre-demo meetings, but the format, timing and location of the on-site demos are not stated here. The bidder would ask when the demos occur and what resources must be committed.

The demo script is described as pre-defined but is not included in this chunk; bidders need to know where the script is published and whether it is fixed or negotiable, since it drives demo preparation effort and staffing.
The pre-demo meeting is mentioned but no date, format or attendance requirement is given; bidders would ask when it occurs and whether attendance is mandatory.

The proposal must follow "the order defined in the table below", but the table is not included in this text, so the bidder cannot know the required proposal section order; the bidder would ask for the table or the prescribed proposal outline.

The page limit is stated twice with different wording ("should not exceed 100 pages" versus a mandatory 100 total pages excluding sample contracts), leaving unclear whether the limit is mandatory and whether the Requirements document in Word counts toward it.

The question deadline and the date the City posts answers are only referenced as being in Section 3, so the bidder cannot tell from this text whether the email question deadline is the same as the proposal due date; the bidder would ask for the exact question cut-off date and time.

The required proposal sections are said to be "outlined below" but the list is not in this text, and the boundary between acceptable marketing material and required product/company description is undefined; the bidder would ask for the definitive section list and whether product brochures or screenshots are permitted.

The pricing must cover "the user counts defined in this RFP", but this chunk does not state those counts, so the bidder cannot size the software pricing without knowing the named/authorized user quantities.

The text says pricing "should be comprehensive including all taxes", which is a soft 'should' but is treated as a hard pricing constraint; bidders would ask whether all applicable taxes must be embedded in the quoted prices or shown separately.

The text requires references 'similar in size and scope to the City's project' but does not state the City's project size, scope or user counts, so bidders cannot judge which references qualify; the bidder would ask what size and scope criteria will be applied.

The security administration item lists 'SSO, SAML, etic', which appears to be a typo or truncated term, leaving unclear what additional capability is being requested; the bidder would ask what 'etic' refers to.

The text says a submitted document with blank responses "may be considered incomplete and rejected" but does not say whether a rating of 0 (Not available) still requires a supporting comment; bidders would ask whether every item, including unavailable ones, needs a narrative comment.

The rating scale defines 4 as available "out of the box or with configuration included in thisproposal", but it is unclear whether configuration effort must be priced in the proposal or is assumed included at no extra cost; bidders would ask how configuration is to be priced.

The 100-word limit is stated for each line-item response, but the sample answer itself says "(limit to 100 words)" inside the cell; it is unclear whether the limit applies to the whole cell including the rating or only the comment text, and whether exceeding it disqualifies the response.

The sample row shows a requirement (R) and a sample response, but it is unclear whether the vendor must reproduce the requirement text, the rating column, or both, and what rating scale or values are expected in the "Rating and Comment" column.
The deadline for submitting written questions is only given by reference to Section 3 – Timeline, which is not in this text; a bidder would ask for the actual question-submission date and time.

It is unclear whether proposers must formally acknowledge each addendum in their proposal (and in what form) or merely incorporate its content, since the text only says failure to acknowledge will not relieve responsibility.

The submission deadline is given only by reference to Section 3 – Timeline and the "project schedule", which are not in this text; a bidder would ask for the exact date and time for electronic submission.

The text does not say what form the advance notice of proprietary/confidential material must take (e.g., a marked schedule or form) or how far in advance it must be given; a bidder would ask for the required format and timing.

The insurance section requires a certification of insurance and an underwriter's endorsement but states no coverage types, limits or additional insured parties, so the bidder cannot price the insurance. The bidder would ask what coverages, limits and additional insured wording are required.

The template requires a separate pricing sheet per deployment option, but this chunk does not identify which deployment options exist (e.g., SaaS vs. on-premise), so the bidder cannot know how many pricing sheets to prepare. The bidder would ask which deployment options must be priced.

The template lists "Project and Grant Accounting" twice among the Financial Modules, leaving unclear whether two separate line items are expected or it is a duplication. The bidder would ask whether to price it once or twice.

The template requires "Assumptions" for each pricing block but does not say what level of detail or format is expected, which affects effort and page count. The bidder would ask what assumption detail is required.

The exhibit does not state whether the three references must be live on the same ERP product/modules being proposed, or whether any current customer of the bidder qualifies; the bidder would ask what eligibility criteria the references must meet.

The exhibit does not say whether the references must be from public-sector or similarly sized organizations, nor what "Population" means (e.g., residents served vs. employees); the bidder would ask for the intended definition and any minimum size threshold.

The table does not state how many prior customer references are required or whether the two slots are a minimum or a maximum; a bidder would ask whether exactly two references are required or whether more may be submitted.

The fields "Population" and "Number of Employees" are undefined as to whether they refer to the reference customer's organisation or to the population served by the software; a bidder would ask which figure is expected.

gaps.description: The Requirements template that best-of-breed respondents must complete is referenced as being in Section 6 but is not included in this text.
A separate Requirements document listing the ERP modules and functionality is provided with the RFP and is needed to scope the solution.
The chunk refers to tables outlining the City's current environment and the solutions in scope, but no such tables appear in this text; the bidder needs them to determine which systems are in scope.
A Demo Script document that will be used for on-site software demos is to be included with the notification to selected finalist vendors.
The Pricing Summary form that must be completed for the pricing section is an exhibit of the RFP provided separately.
Reference forms the proposal must use for providing customer references are provided in a separate exhibit.
The ERP Requirements document is provided as a separate Word document that the vendor must complete and submit as Section 2 of its proposal; it is not included in this chunk.
